steps.title: Store and reread two media signatures
preconditions: Run the entire existing public command tracer app -- test services discussions-assets. The original 40 HTTP checks execute first in the same isolated Miniflare Worker; four synthetic actors have hashed sessions and the owner/member/viewer belong to a synthetic paid team. No native app, provider login or external account is used.

The existing owner process confines homes/storage, applies the three production D1 migrations, bundles the real Worker and denies unexpected outbound requests. ASSET_MAX_BYTES is the ordinary service setting configured to 12 for this local fixture only. The original PNG is exactly 12 bytes and is deleted before the new chapter.

Before the appended chapter, reset only this synthetic team billing fixture to active for one hour. The member session remains authorized, under the 120/hour upload rate limit. Requests use actual loopback HTTP, no production-function calls or HTTP response stubs.

JPEG and WebP are inert 3-byte and 12-byte signature fixtures, not decoded images. Only the asset table and R2 keys/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata are compared for nonmutation. Security rate counters may change; there is no entire-database, all-R2-metadata, quota-counter, race, reconciliation, provider, native or measured-line-coverage claim.
actions: Complete the existing discussions/assets journey assertions, including deletion of the original PNG and the synthetic subscription-lapse discussion checks; then reactivate that fixture team.
PUT the 3-byte JPEG and exact-12-byte WebP signatures with valid distinct asset IDs and parameterized Content-Type, retry each with bare Content-Type, then viewer GET and HEAD both.
Capture and validate exactly two ready asset rows plus their matching R2 keys, bytes, contentType and sha256/projectId/teamId metadata.

expectations.description: Both distinct media signatures are created once, retry successfully, and viewer GET/HEAD return exact bytes, MIME type, length and digest headers; HEAD has no body.
Exactly two ready rows retain valid supplied asset IDs, project/team/uploader, MIME and byte count, and match the two R2 contents and specified metadata.

mappings.why: The JPEG and RIFF/WEBP signature branches select the persisted and returned media types. This is signature recognition, not codec decoding or every malformed signature alternative.

steps.title: Refuse malformed and oversized media without orphan storage
preconditions: Run the entire existing public command tracer app -- test services discussions-assets. The original 40 HTTP checks execute first in the same isolated Miniflare Worker; four synthetic actors have hashed sessions and the owner/member/viewer belong to a synthetic paid team. No native app, provider login or external account is used.

The existing owner process confines homes/storage, applies the three production D1 migrations, bundles the real Worker and denies unexpected outbound requests. ASSET_MAX_BYTES is the ordinary service setting configured to 12 for this local fixture only. The original PNG is exactly 12 bytes and is deleted before the new chapter.

Before the appended chapter, reset only this synthetic team billing fixture to active for one hour. The member session remains authorized, under the 120/hour upload rate limit. Requests use actual loopback HTTP, no production-function calls or HTTP response stubs.

JPEG and WebP are inert 3-byte and 12-byte signature fixtures, not decoded images. Only the asset table and R2 keys/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata are compared for nonmutation. Security rate counters may change; there is no entire-database, all-R2-metadata, quota-counter, race, reconciliation, provider, native or measured-line-coverage claim.

The original PNG has been deleted, so invalid-asset-id targets a missing replica and reaches id validation rather than existing-ready retry. JPEG/WebP sentinels remain ready. All refusal inputs are at most 13 bytes; only the two size cases exceed the configured 12-byte cap.
actions: PUT empty bytes; PUT a three-byte truncated PNG signature; PUT JPEG bytes declared WebP; PUT JPEG at an incorrect all-zero digest; PUT the deleted valid PNG with an invalid space-containing asset ID.
PUT a valid PNG signature plus one extra byte, first as a known-length 13-byte Buffer and then as a two-chunk ReadableStream with no supplied Content-Length.
POST the deleted valid PNG to the asset route; after each of all eight refusals compare every asset row and the R2 keys/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata with the two-sentinel baseline.
After all refusals, viewer GET both original media signatures and compare exact bytes.

expectations.description: The eight named inputs return exact status/code/message and standard JSON/no-store/nosniff headers. Every refusal leaves all asset rows and R2 keys/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata unchanged, and both sentinel media remain readable.
For each named refusal the HTTP body is exactly {error:{code,message}}, with its independently specified status and JSON/no-store/nosniff headers; no details or internal-error behavior is claimed.

mappings.why: Truncated PNG matches none of the signature branches and receives invalid_media before any asset reservation.
The configured 12-byte cap, empty bytes, MIME disagreement and digest disagreement are exercised through authorized PUT. Default/max limits, quota and racing authorization changes are excluded.
The deleted PNG has no existing-ready row, so its invalid supplied asset ID reaches validation. The successful prior uploads retain valid IDs.
The known-length 13-byte request exceeds this fixture limit of 12 and returns the exact public 413 response. Invalid/negative Content-Length values are not claimed.

The streamed 13-byte request is sent without a supplied length; bounded stream accumulation supports rejection with unchanged media storage. No transport-chunk segmentation or cancellation side-effect claim.
A space in an otherwise bounded string asset ID is rejected, whereas the punctuation-bearing valid asset IDs are retained in ready rows. Full ID/type/length matrix excluded.
APIError and assertion support preserving exact named error status/code/message through the public HTTP route. Optional details and unexpected internal errors are excluded.
The APIError response arm serializes exactly the requested code/message and status with details absent. The unrelated internal-error arm is excluded.

actions: Owner DELETE the JPEG and verify public missing-asset response, exact surviving WebP GET, and full remaining asset/R2 state equals only its captured sentinel.

Owner DELETE WebP twice, require both responses successful, and assert empty assets table/R2 listing. Require all twelve new mutation/refusal labels and zero unexpected outbound attempts before owned process/state cleanup.

expectations.description: Removing JPEG preserves the complete WebP row and specified R2 content/metadata; removing WebP then repeating DELETE leaves no rows or objects.

mappings.why: Successful owner deletion removes only the selected object key and matching deleting row. The independently retained WebP sentinel distinguishes indiscriminate cleanup. No stale-delete or concurrent replacement claim.
